commitResults.messageTitle: Update README with new features and examples
commitResults.messageBody:
Add README docs for find, persistence, exit

The README previously only documented features 1-3 (add, list,
delete). Features 4-6 (find, automatic data persistence, exit)
were implemented but undocumented, leaving users without guidance
on how to search records or what happens to their data between
sessions.

Document the find command's syntax and matching behaviour, explain
that persistence is automatic with no user action required, and
describe the exit command, following the same format already used
for features 1-3.

commitResults.messageTitle: Fix heading level for features 4-6 in README
commitResults.messageBody:
Features 4-6 (find, persistence, exit) were added as H2 headings
instead of H3, causing them to render with an underline that
doesn't match the H3 styling used by features 1-3.

Change the three headings from ## to ### to match the existing
heading hierarchy.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add user stories 17-32 to Developer Guide
commitResults.messageBody:
The User stories table only had stories for extension-style and
nice-to-have behaviour (undo, shortcuts, anomaly detection, etc.).
None of the core CRUD commands - add, list, delete, find, automatic
persistence, exit - had a story, and the table ended with a
"{More to be added}" placeholder for the second half of the
assigned stories.

Add 14 stories covering the missing core commands as must-haves,
plus should-have and nice-to-have stories for filtering, team
roster views, sorting, leave-status lookup, delete confirmation,
and workforce-connectivity checks, following the same Priority /
As a / I can / So that I can format already used in the table.

These fill out the "17-32" half of the user stories assigned in
Week 7, matching priorities to what's actually implemented versus
still planned, per the course's requirement that the DG cover the
full product scope rather than just the current iteration.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add remaining user stories to Developer Guide
commitResults.messageBody:
The previous commit only included part of the new user stories -
a few rows from the intended set did not get copied in correctly.

Add the missing rows so the table includes the full set of stories
covering the core CRUD commands and the remaining busy/careful/
long-time user scenarios assigned for this half of the Developer
Guide.

Rename the AB3 Person classes to Employee, including the model
package, UI, storage and tests, to match HuntR's domain.

Rename only, no behaviour change. JSON storage now uses the key
"employees" instead of "persons".

commitResults.messageTitle: Add id, department and role to Employee
commitResults.messageBody:
Give Employee the fields from the feature spec: employee ID, name,
phone, email, department and role. Remove address and remark, along
with the tutorial's remark command, since HuntR does not use them.

Identify employees by their employee ID instead of their name. IDs
are 1 to 20 letters, digits, hyphens or underscores and are compared
case-insensitively, so company-specific ID schemes are supported.
Department and role accept common punctuation such as "R&D".

Update the add and edit commands, storage, UI card, sample data and
tests for the new fields. Employee IDs cannot be edited.

Tags are not part of the agreed HuntR employee fields or of the add,
list and delete outputs, so remove them: the t/ option of add and
edit, the tags shown on the employee card and in command messages,
and their storage.

Also delete src/main/java/seedu/address/model/util/92624417, a
duplicate of SampleDataUtil that was added by mistake.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add employee rules for names, duplicates and errors
commitResults.messageBody:
Make the add command follow the feature spec and the Week 8 guidance.

Names may contain relation words such as s/o, d/o and a/l, as well as
hyphens, apostrophes and non-Latin letters. Words like d/o are treated
as part of the name instead of the department prefix. Extra spaces in
names are collapsed.

Reject an employee whose ID already exists with the spec's message.
Add an employee whose name only differs in case or spacing from an
existing one, but warn the user so a duplicate can be spotted.

Accept more phone layouts, such as +65 6123-4567 and labels in
brackets. Reject unknown parameters, and give separate error messages
for blank, too long, too few digits and invalid characters.
Implement exit command
Implement find employees by name

commitResults.messageTitle: Fix name, phone and department parsing edge cases
commitResults.messageBody:
Only treat relation words such as d/o and s/o as part of a name when
they appear inside the name field. A department such as "O & G" that
follows other fields was wrongly read as name text.

Accept combining marks in names, so names such as the Tamil name
written with a virama and an accent stored as a separate character
are valid. Store names in their standard Unicode form so that both
spellings are the same name, including in the similar-name warning.

Check phone numbers with a loop instead of a regular expression. The
regular expression overflowed the stack on very long input.
Improve find command input validation

commitResults.messageBody:

commitResults.messageTitle: Add filter command for department and role
commitResults.messageBody:
Add filter [d/DEPARTMENT] [r/ROLE] to show only the employees whose
department and role match all the given values, ignoring case and
matching whole words as find does.

Reject missing, blank, invalid, repeated and unknown parameters with a
specific message followed by the usage. Filtering only changes the
displayed list; list shows every employee again.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add sort command for the displayed list
commitResults.messageBody:
Add sort FIELD, where FIELD is id, name, department or role, to show
the employees in ascending order, ignoring case. Employees with an
equal value are ordered by employee ID.

Sort a view of the list in the model so that the stored order is
never changed. list shows the saved order again.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add asc and desc order to sort command
commitResults.messageBody:
The feature spec asks for ascending and descending sorting, but sort
only supported ascending order.

Add an optional asc or desc argument after the field, defaulting to
ascending. Employees with an equal value stay ordered by ID from A to
Z, also in descending order.

Ignore accents when sorting so that names such as Emile and Émile are
placed together, instead of accented letters coming after z. Use
Locale.ROOT in SortField#toString so the field names do not depend on
the language of the computer.

Update the user guide and help text, and add tests for the new order,
accented names, editing and deleting under a sort, and list restoring
the saved order.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extend filter with name, ID and OR matching
commitResults.messageBody:
The filter command only accepted department and role, rejected
repeated prefixes, and could not find words next to punctuation. The
feature spec asks for filtering by name, ID, department and role, with
several values of one field matching any of them.

Add n/ and id/ criteria. Criteria of different fields must all match.
Repeating a prefix, such as d/Sales d/Finance, matches any of its
values, while the words inside one value must all match.

Split values and fields into words on spaces and punctuation, keeping
& and ', so that R&D, Asia and Engineer (Backend) can be found. Check
the typed values as search words instead of as complete departments or
roles, so that r/(Backend) is accepted.

Update the user guide and help text, and add tests for the new
criteria, OR matching, punctuation and archived employees.

The undo and redo tests read the filter predicate by casting the
displayed employee list to FilteredList. The displayed list is now a
SortedList that wraps the FilteredList, so unwrap it with getSource()
in those tests.

commitResults.messageTitle: Enable assertions when running with Gradle
commitResults.messageBody:
Gradle turns assertions off for the run task, so an assert statement
that fails while the app is run with ./gradlew run is silently
ignored. Assertions were only checked by the tests.

Enable them for the run task so that a broken assumption is reported
when the app is run during development.

The application still reported V1.3 at startup. Update VERSION so
that the jar of the v1.4 release shows the right version.

commitResults.messageTitle: Configure run task lazily and document scope
commitResults.messageBody:
Use tasks.named so that the run task is configured only when it is
needed, and so that its type is explicit.

Add a comment that assertions are enabled for ./gradlew run only, as
the generated JAR and java -jar still run without assertions.

commitResults.messageTitle: Colour departments and results in the UI
commitResults.messageBody:
The employee list and the result box are plain, so it takes effort to
tell departments apart and to see at a glance whether a command worked.

Show the department of an employee as a chip. A department always has
the same colour, and a department without a fixed colour gets one from
a small palette by its name. Show an Archived badge for archived
employees. Show the result of a command with a green stripe, and an
error with a red stripe and red text.

Only the user interface changes. Add tests for the department colours.

The card showed seven lines of labelled text, so a screen fits only a
few employees and the important values are hard to find.

Show a round avatar with the initials of the employee, in the colour
of their department. Show the name with a small monospace ID, then the
role, then the email and phone on one muted line, without labels. Show
the manager of an employee as a chip with their ID, and show nothing
when there is no manager.

Only the user interface changes. Add tests for the initials.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add command history and Tab completion
commitResults.messageBody:
A command with a typo has to be typed again from the start, and every
command word has to be typed in full.

Go through the commands that were typed with the up and down keys, and
keep the text that was being typed. Complete the command word with the
Tab key, as far as the command words agree. Clear the command box with
the Escape key. Remember a command that gave an error too, so that it
can be brought back and corrected.

Add tests for the history and the completion, and a test that the
command words are the commands of the parser and the help summary.
Describe the keys in the user guide.

commitResults.messageTitle: Fit long values on the employee card
commitResults.messageBody:
At the narrowest window, a long name or email made the card wider than
the list. The ID and the phone number were cut off and the list scrolled
sideways.

Make a card as wide as its cell and no wider, so that long text is cut
short with an ellipsis, and never cut the ID. Show the phone number
before the email, because the email is the part that is long. Show the
whole name, role, department or contact line in a tooltip.

Only the user interface changes.
Redesign the employee card layout

commitResults.messageTitle: Add tests for filter combined with sort
commitResults.messageBody:
The review of the sort command asked for tests that use filter and sort
together, which was only possible after both were merged. Each command
was tested alone and with find, but not with the other, and not with
undo.

Test filter then sort, sort then filter, and that both orders show the
same employees in the same order. Test that list shows every employee
in the saved order again, that the stored data does not change, and that
an employee whose sort key is edited moves inside the filtered
employees. Test that undo and redo keep both the sort and the filter.

Only tests change.

commitResults.messageTitle: Update the class diagrams for v1.4
commitResults.messageBody:
The class diagrams did not show what was added in v1.4 for sorting and

Show CommandHistory, CommandCompleter, DepartmentColour and Initials in

commitResults.messageTitle: Match the words of a name in find
commitResults.messageBody:
The find command split a name at spaces only, so a word followed by a
comma, a full stop or a hyphen could not be found: find Tan did not find
Tan, Ah Kow. It did not ignore accents, and its message for an invalid
keyword did not say which keyword was invalid.

Split the name and each keyword into words with the method that filter
uses, so that find and filter agree, and ignore accents in both. Let any
kind of space separate keywords, and name the first invalid keyword in
the message. Update the user guide and the developer guide.

commitResults.messageTitle: Allow accents in a department and a role
commitResults.messageBody:
A department or a role with an accent, such as Soporte técnico, was
rejected, although the message said that letters are allowed. The
validation used a class that matches only the letters of English, while
a name accepts any letter.

Accept the same letters as a name in a department and a role, and store
them in the same normalised form, so that an accent typed as a separate
mark is the same department. Describe the rules in the user guide.

commitResults.messageTitle: Suggest the closest command for a typo
commitResults.messageBody:
An unknown command such as List or fliter only said that the command
was unknown, and the user guide did not say that command words are in
lowercase.

Find the command that is closest to the unknown word, with a new class
that knows all the command words, and add a line to the message that
says which command may have been meant. When the word only differs in
letter case, the line also says that command words are lowercase. Use
the same list of command words for the Tab key. Update the user guide.

commitResults.messageTitle: Resize result box to fit its message
commitResults.messageBody:
The result box was fixed at 100 pixels, so only the first lines of a
long result such as stats could be seen without scrolling a small
box. Long lines were also cut off instead of wrapped.

Make the box as high as its text, between 100 and 350 pixels, and
wrap long lines. The height is worked out from the text and the width
of the box, so it is updated when the window is resized. A short
message keeps the box at 100 pixels as before.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document filter and sort in the UG and DG
commitResults.messageBody:
The DG had no section for the filter and sort commands, and the error
tables of both commands in the UG showed the wrong message.

Add implementation sections with sequence diagrams, use cases and
manual test steps for both commands to the DG. In the UG, correct the
error messages, and state that a new filter replaces the earlier one,
that the sort order is kept by filter, and that it is not remembered
after HuntR is closed.

commitResults.messageTitle: Sort the numbers in a value by their value
commitResults.messageBody:
The sort command compared the values character by character, so E10
came before E2 and Level 10 before Level 2. An employee ID does not have
to be padded with zeros, so IDs such as E1, E2 and E10 are normal.

Compare a number inside a value by its value with a new comparator, for
the four sort fields and for the ordering by ID of equal values. Letter
case and accents are still ignored. Describe the order in the user
guide.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add hashCode to the filter and sort commands
commitResults.messageBody:
FilterCommand and SortCommand overrode equals but not hashCode, so two
equal commands had different hash codes. A HashSet or HashMap of
commands could not find an equal command, which breaks the contract
between equals and hashCode.

Override hashCode with the same fields as equals: the predicate for
FilterCommand, and the field and the order for SortCommand. Add tests
that equal commands have the same hash code and are found in a HashSet.
Allow accents in a department and a role

commitResults.messageTitle: Share the vertical space with the result test
commitResults.messageBody:
The test of the result box height repeated the value of
VERTICAL_SPACE as the number 40, so it would fail without a clear
reason if the space around the text is changed.

Make VERTICAL_SPACE package-private, as MIN_HEIGHT and MAX_HEIGHT
already are, and use it in the test.

commitResults.messageTitle: Make command hints stricter for short words
commitResults.messageBody:
A word of four letters could be two changes away from a command, so
quit gave the hint "Did you mean edit?" and sear gave clear. Such a
hint can mislead someone who meant another command, such as exit.

Allow one change for a word of up to five letters, and two changes
only from six letters, where a typo is less likely to hit another
command. Also rename sameLetter to substitutionCost, which is 0 when
the letters are equal, and swapped to isSwapped, to read as a boolean.

commitResults.messageTitle: Work out the keyword words once in find
commitResults.messageBody:
The predicate split every keyword into words again for each employee
it tested, although the keywords do not change after the predicate is
created. With a large roster the same work was done for every test.

Work out the words of the keywords in the constructor and keep the
keywords only for equals and toString. A keyword without a word is
dropped there, so test no longer has to check for it.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use employee ID to select employee in edit command
commitResults.messageBody:
The edit command identifies the target employee by its index in the
displayed list, while delete is moving to employee IDs. Using different
ways to pick an employee for the two commands is confusing.

Let's make edit take id/EMPLOYEE_ID instead:

* Parse a required id/ prefix in EditCommandParser and reject any
  preamble, such as an index.
* Look up the employee in the full employee list, so employees hidden
  by a find filter can still be edited.
* Report "No employee with ID X was found." when no employee matches.

The employee ID itself is still not editable.
Delete employee

commitResults.messageTitle: Fix failing delete parser test for too-long IDs
commitResults.messageBody:
DeleteCommandParserTest expects the general employee ID constraint
message for a 21-character ID. However, ParserUtil#parseEmployeeId now
reports a more specific message when an ID is valid apart from its
length, so the test fails on master.

Let's keep the more specific message, and test the too-long ID
separately against it.

commitResults.messageTitle: Share name relation word and unknown parameter handling with edit
commitResults.messageBody:
The edit command reads "d/o" in a name such as "Nur Aisha d/o Ali" as
the department prefix, silently splitting the name. It also folds
unknown parameters such as x/foo into the previous value. The add
command already handles both cases, but its logic is private to
AddCommandParser.

Let's move that logic into a package-private ArgumentPreprocessor
class, and use it from both AddCommandParser and EditCommandParser.
Relation words are still only treated as name text inside the name
field, so "d/O & G" after another field is read as a department.

Remove leftover AB3 branding
Update User Guide command sections for HuntR

commitResults.messageTitle: Fix user guide URL in help window
commitResults.messageBody: The GitHub Pages URL was missing the semester (s1) and returned 404.
Rebrand User Guide general sections, README and UI screenshot to HuntR

The upcoming import and export commands need to read and write CSV
files. Names, departments and roles may contain commas, which would
split a value into two columns if written as is.

Let's add CsvUtil, which quotes values that contain commas, quotes or
line breaks, and reads such values back, as spreadsheet programs do.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add CSV file path parsing to ParserUtil
commitResults.messageBody:
The import and export commands take a file path from the user. HuntR
must not read or write files outside the folder it runs from.

Let's add ParserUtil#parseCsvFilePath, which accepts only relative
paths that stay inside that folder and end in .csv.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add export and import commands for CSV files
commitResults.messageBody:
Users cannot load employee records from a spreadsheet or take a copy
of their data out of HuntR.

Let's,
* add export FILE_PATH, which writes all employees to a CSV file with
  the header id,name,phone,email,department,role
* add import FILE_PATH, which adds every employee in such a file
* list both commands in the help window

Import checks every row with the same rules as the add command before
adding anything, so a bad row or a repeated employee ID leaves the
records unchanged. The error names the row as a spreadsheet numbers
it, so users can find it easily.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document export and import commands in user guide

commitResults.messageBody:
Users who want a safe copy of their data before a risky change, such
as editing the data file or importing many employees, have to copy the
data file by hand.

Let's add a backup command that saves the current employee data to
data/backups/huntr-YYYYMMDD-HHmmss.json and shows the path.

The backup is written from the data in memory, in the same format as
the data file, so it works even before the data file is first created.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document backup command in user guide

commitResults.messageBody:
A double quote anywhere in a CSV line switches quote mode on or off.
A value such as A"li"ce is therefore read as Alice, which changes the
supplied data and lets a value that should fail validation through.

Let's accept a double quote only where CSV allows it: at the start of
a value, just before the comma or line end that closes it, or doubled
inside a quoted value. Anything else is an error, so import rejects
the whole file.

commitResults.messageTitle: Check real CSV file location before import or export
commitResults.messageBody:
The path check in ParserUtil only looks at the path as typed. A path
through a symbolic link to a folder outside the HuntR folder passes it,
so export can write and import can read outside that folder.

Let's,
* add FileUtil#isInsideFolder, which follows symbolic links in the
  existing part of a path
* add CsvFileCommand, which import and export now extend, to resolve
  the path against the app folder and check it just before file access
* add tests with symbolic links, skipped where links are not supported

The check happens when the command runs rather than in the parser, as
the files and links can change between parsing and running.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document quote and shortcut rules for import and export
Test backup with an active employee filter
commitResults.messageBody:
The user guide says a backup contains all employees, including those
hidden by find, but no test covers a filtered list.

Let's add a test that backs up while a filter is active, then checks
that the backup has every employee and the filter is unchanged.

Keep archived status in CSV import and export

Export writes archived employees without their archived status, so
importing the file brings them back as active employees.

Let's,
* add an archived column (true or false) to exported files
* read it on import, where blank means false
* still accept files without the column, importing everyone as active

Files made before this change, or by hand with the original header,
keep working.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add import sequence diagram to Developer Guide
commitResults.messageBody:
The Developer Guide does not describe how the CSV import and export
commands work, so developers have to read the code to learn why a
failed import adds no employees.

Let's,
* add a sequence diagram for a successful import
* add a CSV import and export section that explains the checks done
  before the model changes and links the diagram

commitResults.messageTitle: Collapse repeated spaces in department and role
commitResults.messageBody:
Department and role values keep any double spaces typed inside them.
A value such as "Human  Resources" is then stored, listed and counted
by stats as a different department from "Human Resources", although
the two look the same on screen.

Names already reduce repeated spaces to one.

Let's,
* reduce runs of whitespace inside department and role to one space
  when parsing them
* add a parser test and a UG note for this behaviour

Fixes #144

commitResults.messageTitle: Check: Flag emails that differ only in letter case
commitResults.messageBody:
The check command compares emails exactly as stored, so
"alice@example.com" and "ALICE@example.com" are not reported as a
shared email.

Both addresses reach the same inbox, so this is the kind of data-entry
error check is meant to catch.

Let's,
* compare emails in lower case when counting shared emails, while
  still showing each email as stored
* keep comparing phone numbers exactly
* update the tests and the UG

Fixes #146

commitResults.messageTitle: Edit: Reject edits that change nothing
commitResults.messageBody:
An edit whose values are all the same as the employee's current values
reports "Edited employee" and adds an undo step, although nothing has
changed. Users cannot tell that the edit had no effect, e.g. if they
meant to change a different field.

Let's,
* reject such an edit with a message that names the employee, so
  nothing is saved or added to the undo history
* update the tests that used a no-op edit, and add tests for edits
  with no fields and with unchanged values
* describe the new message in the UG

Fixes #148

commitResults.messageTitle: EditCommandTest: Lower-case IDs with the root locale
commitResults.messageBody:
The codebase lower-cases IDs with Locale.ROOT so that the result does
not depend on the default locale of the machine running the tests.

commitResults.messageTitle: Keep a copy of a data file that cannot be loaded
commitResults.messageBody:
When the data file is invalid, HuntR starts with no employees and only
logs a warning. The next command, even help, saves the empty list over
the file, so a single typo in the file deletes the whole roster without
the user ever being told.

Let's,
* copy the unreadable file to unreadable-addressbook.json in the same
  folder before anything can overwrite it
* show a warning in the result box at startup that names the copy and
  explains how to restore it, or asks the user to back up the file if
  the copy fails
* update the UG caution on editing the data file

Fixes #143

commitResults.messageTitle: Tell users to replace the data file with the fixed copy
commitResults.messageBody:
The warning and the UG say to rename the fixed copy to
addressbook.json. A file with that name already exists, so the rename
is refused or has to replace it anyway.

Let's say "use it to replace" the data file instead.

commitResults.messageTitle: Stats: Sort tied groups alphabetically ignoring case
commitResults.messageBody:
When two departments or roles have the same count, stats orders them
case-sensitively, so every uppercase name comes before every lowercase
one. For example, "apple" is listed after "Human Resources".

Users expect alphabetical order regardless of how a name was typed.

Let's,
* break ties in alphabetical order that ignores letter case, and fall
  back to the case-sensitive order for names that differ only in case
* update the UG and DG descriptions of the tie order

Fixes #145

commitResults.messageTitle: Show the manager in employee result messages
commitResults.messageBody:
Result messages for commands such as edit list an employee's ID, name,
contact details, department and role, but not their manager. After
"edit id/E0001 m/E0004" or "edit id/E0001 m/", the message is the
same, so users cannot confirm a manager change from the result.

Let's,
* append the manager ID to the formatted employee when there is one
* add tests for employees with and without a manager
* mention the manager in the UG section on edit

Fixes #147

commitResults.messageTitle: MainApp: Return the startup warning with the model
commitResults.messageBody:
initModelManager sets the startup warning as a side effect, so init
only passes the right warning to the UI if it calls initModelManager
first. The UI also treats an empty string as "no warning".

Let's,
* return the model and the warning together in a StartupData record
* pass the warning to the UI as an Optional

commitResults.messageTitle: Stats: Order tied labels the same way as sort
commitResults.messageBody:
Ties in stats are ordered by String.CASE_INSENSITIVE_ORDER, which puts
accented labels after every unaccented one (Émile after Zebra) and
compares numbers as text (Level 10 before Level 2). The sort command
ignores accents and compares numbers by value, so the two commands
list the same departments in different orders.

Let's,
* expose the value order of sort as SortField.VALUE_ORDER
* use it to order tied labels in stats

commitResults.messageTitle: UG: Note the manager in every employee result message
commitResults.messageBody:
The success messages of add, delete, archive and unarchive also show
the manager, as they share the same format as edit. The UG mentions
it only under edit, and the delete section lists the fields without
the manager.

Let's note it once in the command format notes, and add the manager
to the fields listed for delete.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add immutable history snapshots and checkpoints
commitResults.messageBody:
Employee data has no retained states or rollback checkpoints. Reversing
changes requires complete stored values and access to the redo tail.

Add immutable ordered snapshots and stable checkpoints that preserve raw
ID spelling, employee order and archive status. Share immutable
snapshots to keep checkpoint capture linear in employee count and
history length.

commitResults.messageTitle: Wire employee history into the model
commitResults.messageBody:
Model mutations have no explicit history lifecycle, and additions cannot
be recorded for later reversal.

Expose commit, undo, redo and checkpoint operations through the model.
Preserve working-data replacement, effective views and ordinary model
equality.

Classify data-changing commands and record successful additions once.
Adapt the model stub and add tests for history, checkpoint stability,
raw stored values and observable-list identity.

Employee edits update working data without recording a history step.

Mark edits as data-changing and commit once after all field updates.
Keep the existing success message and filter reset so identical edits
remain successful while the model preserves redo.

Deleting an employee removes the record without retaining a history
step.

Mark deletions as data-changing and commit after removal so active,
archived and hidden employees can be restored with their stored values
and position.

Clearing active employees has no history entry for restoring the roster.

Mark clear as data-changing and commit after removal. Let the model skip
identical states so empty clears preserve redo while keeping the
existing success message and filter behavior.

commitResults.messageTitle: Record each CSV import as one history step
commitResults.messageBody:
CSV imports add employees individually, but users need to reverse an
entire import as one operation.

Mark import as data-changing and commit only after all rows have been
added. Retain a complete snapshot so redo can restore the imported
records without rereading the CSV.

Archiving changes employee status without recording a reversible step.

Mark archive as data-changing and commit after the status transition so
undo can restore the active employee without changing existing
validation or success messages.

Restoring an archived employee changes status without a history entry.

Mark unarchive as data-changing and commit after the status transition
so undo can restore archived status while preserving the existing
validation and view behavior.

Recorded employee states are not accessible through the command parser.
Users need one-step navigation with predictable syntax and boundary
errors.

Add lowercase undo and redo commands that preserve the current view and
navigate snapshots without creating new entries. Reject arguments before
checking history availability.

Test exact parsing errors, mixed command sequences, whole-import
reversal, raw ID reuse and redo after the source CSV changes or
disappears.

commitResults.messageTitle: Fix JSON payload test on Windows

while undo and redo only navigate existing snapshots.
